title: Allow more HTTP verbs as method and formmethod
body:
## Problem ##

Currently the only allowed values for the `method` attribute in a `<form>` element—and the `formmethod` attribute in a `<button>` element—are `GET`, `POST` and `dialog`.

As a crawler I would like buttons and forms to actually tell me *which* action they perform and *how* they will perform it. As a crawler I spent all this time looking at API documentation for a web app. Now I am going to help a user navigate through it, but none of the `<form>`s and `<button>`s make any sense relative to the documentation. 

By not allowing [all common HTTP request methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods) developers are forced to use non-semantic ways of marking up their forms and buttons, and later use scripts or server hacks to attach the correct behavior. For example:

Instead of:

```html
<button type="submit" formmethod="DELETE" formaction="/api/path/to/resource">
  Delete resource
</button>
```

…a developer must write something like:

```html
<button type="button" data-method="DELETE" data-action="/api/path/to/resource">
  Delete resource
</button>
```
…and recreate the submit behavior with a script: 

```js
document.querySelectorAll("[type='button']").forEach(button => {
  button.addEventListener("click", () => {
    const { action, method } = button.dataset;
    fetch(action, { method });
  });
});
```

Of course the above solution will not work without javascript, so a smart developer might use a server hack instead and run some proxy endpoints:

```html
<button type="submit" formmethod="POST" formaction="/api/hack/path/to/resource?method=delete">
  Delete resource
</button>
```

However the problem here is that we are forcing developers away from creating clean APIs and it is unlikely that they will document these hack endpoints. As a crawler I find that annoying.

## Proposal ##

In addition to the [current allowed values](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#attr-fs-formmethod) for the `method` and `formmethod` attributes on `<form>` and `<button>` elements respectively, allow the following values:

* `head`
* `put`
* `delete`
* `connect`
* `options`
* `trace`
* `patch`

When submitting a form—or clicking a button—with one of these methods the browser should behave just like it currently does with the `get` or `post` values, except use the specified method for the request.
